newsitem.title: USA: Dow drops after stumbling on way to 8,000 level.
newsitem.headline: Dow drops after stumbling on way to 8,000 level.

text.p: The Dow Jones industrial average descended Wednesday after stumbling in an early attempt at the 8,000-point level.
At 1 p.m. EDT/1700 GMT, the Dow was off 38.91 points at 7,923.40, having pulled back from a high of 7,991.26.
In the broader market, declining issues led advances 14-12 on heavy volume of 316 million shares on the New York Stock Exchange.
But technology stocks were strong, boosted by higher-than-expected results from technology giant Motorola Inc. and expectations for more positive results.
The Nasdaq composite index, which is laden with tech stocks, gained 9.07 points to 1,494.17.
Analysts said investors were worried that portfolio managers would start to sell stocks once the Dow hit 8,000.

"My guess is that a lot of portfolio managers have 8,000 as a target level to sell a bit," said Michael Metz, chief investment strategist at Oppenheimer & Co. "I doubt the 8,000 mark is going to trigger many new buyers."
Peter Coolidge, senior equity trader at Brean Murray & Co. said: "As we get closer to the 8,000 level, the market gets nervous. The problem is -- what happens after we reach 8,000?"

Among the 30-stock Dow components, International Paper Co. slipped 1-11/16 to 54-5/16 after surging Tuesday on news that it would slash its work force, close struggling operations and sell off $1 billion in assets.
Philip Morris Cos., another Dow component, fell 1-1/16 in active trading to 43-3/8, after President Clinton criticised some elements of the proposed tobacco settlement.
"We are entering a period of sumer doldrums, waiting for (second) quarter earnings," said John Cleland, chief investment strategist at Security Benefit Group of Companies.
"The market is totally dominated by individual names," he said. "There just isn't any other big news out there."
Technology stocks ran higher after Motorola reported its second quarter earnings.
"Techs are acting well today, and Motorola is setting the pace," Coolidge said.
Motorola stock was up 3-5/8 at 86-3/8 in brisk trading.
Elsewhere, Compaq Computer Corp. rose 2-8/16 to 122-1/16 and chip maker Intel Corp. gained 4-1/8 to 153-3/4.
Intel's rival, Advanced Micro Devices Inc., also rose slightly despite reporting weaker-than-expected second-quarter results. AMD's stock was up 1/8 at 39-1/4.

McDonald's Corp. rose 1-1/16 to 49-13/16, as the company said it would decentralize its U.S. operations into five geographic divisions in an effort to move decision-making and accountability closer to the restaurant level.
